topSignals.title: Quiet day continues — Elcogen now 54 days quiet, Topsoe 79 days; no genuinely new item found in any monitored section today.
topSignals.text: Dedicated English- and German-language searches for both priority stacks, the Tier 2 dedicated rotation (new cycle, round 1: Bloom Energy, FuelCell Energy) and sweep, the Tier 3 dedicated rotation (cycle 9, round 4, completing the full 20-company roster: Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Miura, Delta Electronics, Shell, Denso, Thermax) and two further Tier 3 sweeps, and broad AI-datacenter/hyperscaler, regulation, competing-power, market/financials, research/IP, and scientific-paper checks (English and German) all returned only recycled/already-logged background or out-of-window items. Elcogen News | Topsoe press releases

items.text: Elcogen (priority): No new news-archive item since Sept 21, 2026 (Metrosert cooperation), confirmed via English- and German-language searches today — 54 days quiet. Status unchanged: elcoStack E3000 G2 platform (75% FC electrical efficiency / 90% with heat recovery, 33 kWh/kg H2 SOEC — vendor claims) in volume production at the 360 MW/yr ELCO I Tallinn factory.

Topsoe (priority): No new solid-oxide-specific release since the Aug 27, 2026 H1 2026 results/SOEC pathway reset, confirmed via English- and German-language searches today — 79 days quiet; topsoe.com/press-releases remains dominated by PTX/ammonia/SAF/blue-hydrogen news (most recently a sustainable-aviation-fuel/renewable-diesel technology-partner announcement in Texas), out of SOFC/SOEC scope.

Today's Tier 2 dedicated rotation (Bloom Energy, FuelCell Energy — new cycle, round 1): no new item for either; results repeated Bloom's standing AI-datacenter backlog narrative (Oracle/Project Jupiter, AEP, Nebius, NTT DATA 900 MW) and FuelCell Energy's Fit Energy/Inuverse/StabilityMax background, both recirculated by aggregator sites (enkiai.com) and investor press (webull, 24/7 Wall St.), all pre-dated.

Today's Tier 2 sweep — "Bloom Energy OR FuelCell Energy OR Ceres Power OR Sunfire OR SolydEra": no new item; results repeated the same Bloom/Oracle/AEP/NTT DATA background recirculated across enkiai.com's standing SOFC market-analysis series.

Today's Tier 3 dedicated rotation — cycle 9, round 4, completing the full 20-company roster (Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Miura, Delta Electronics, Shell, Denso, Thermax): no new items for any of the six; results repeated Kawasaki's non-SOFC hydrogen-combustion power-generator news, Miura's 2024-vintage Ceres-licensed 4.2kW CHP launch and maintenance-network background, Delta Electronics' standing off-grid fuel-cell partnership with Centrica, Shell's July 2026 10 MW Ceres SOEC module contract, Denso's standing Nishio-plant SOFC/SOEC demonstration background, and Thermax's 2024 Ceres green-hydrogen/SOEC manufacturing partnership (all pre-dated).
Tier 3 sweep — "Reverion OR Convion OR Hexis OR Doosan Fuel Cell OR SK ecoplant": no new item; recycled the standing Doosan-Reverion $76.7-78M SOFC stack-supply background.

Tier 3 sweep — "OxEon Energy OR Nexceris OR Kawasaki Heavy Industries OR Miura OR Weichai": no new item; recycled the Miura/Ceres 4.2kW launch and Weichai/Ceres manufacturing-licence/CE-certification background.
Competitor roster: SOFC systems for data centers

Bloom Energy: Deployed/signed at multiple named sites — Oracle/Project Jupiter, AEP (1 GW), Brookfield EaaS, Nebius (328 MW/$2.6B), Equinix (>100 MW/19 sites), Aligned "Project Phoenix" (2 GW), Hitachi (Japan), SK Eternix (28 MW, operational), NTT DATA (900 MW, global, shipments from 2027).

FuelCell Energy (incl. HyAxiom-branded products): Signed orders/PPAs — Fit Energy (up to 380 MW), Inuverse Korea (up to 100 MW), Texas CRA (75 MW), SDCL (up to 450 MW). Also hosting a DOE/national-lab-backed R&D testbed (StabilityMax) in Danbury, CT. No named commercial deployment live yet.
Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom: Signed order — US AI data center supply contract (KRW 823.6B); supplies SOFC stacks to Reverion. No named data-center site of its own yet.
Convion: Pipeline-only/pre-commercial under HD Hyundai ownership; no named data-center customer.
SK ecoplant: Pipeline-only; no new named data-center deployment.
Ceres Power's SOFC licensees (Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai): Licensing/pipeline-only; no named data-center deployment via Ceres licensing directly.
Reverion: Pipeline-only — Doosan-supplied SOFC stacks for rSOC power plants (Germany); no named data-center customer yet.
Petra Power: Pre-commercial, no named customer; first infrastructure deployment targeted 2028.
